The lesion showed a narrow zone of transition, appearing hyperintense on proton density-spectral adiabatic inversion recovery (PD-SPAIR) (red arrow), isointense on T1-weighted imaging (T1WI) (yellow arrow), and mildly hyperintense on T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) (blue arrow) with vivid post-contrast enhancement (orange arrow). There was no evidence of periosteal reaction or any soft tissue involvement.

report.source_text:
The patient was undertaken for excision and curettage (Figure 5) of the lesion (black arrow), following which the cavity in the anterior aspect of the tibia was plugged with hydroxyapatite bone blocks and sealed with bone wax (green arrow). Postoperative X-rays confirmed the adequate filling of the cavity with no evidence of breakage in the bone.
Postoperative physiotherapy was started, and the patient had no postoperative complications. Suture removal was done on post-op day 12, and the patient was subsequently discharged and advised for regular follow-up.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old boy presented with a 4-year history of insidious-onset, non-progressive dull aching pain and swelling in the right leg. He had a prior history of tibia fracture from kabaddi trauma 2 years before, managed conservatively with cast for 3 months. MRI imaging revealed a cortical-based diaphyseal lesion in the anterior proximal tibial shaft with a narrow zone of transition, hyperintense on PD-SPAIR, isointense on T1WI, mildly hyperintense on T2WI, and vivid post-contrast enhancement, with no periosteal reaction or soft tissue involvement. A biopsy was performed showing histopathological features of epithelial cells arranged in a palisading pattern with fibrous mesenchymal cells, consistent with adamantinoma. The patient underwent excision and curettage of the lesion with hydroxyapatite bone block filling and bone wax sealing. Postoperative X-rays confirmed adequate cavity filling with no bone breakage. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, with suture removal on post-op day 12 and discharge with follow-up advised.
